Transitions within and between categories

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code
On this page

On this page

  • Configure this run
  • Load data and select trials
  • Match item IDs to categories
  • Plot transitions within and between categories

Given the items still available, how likely is the next recall to stay in the same category or switch categories? Each participant contributes a probability for each type of transition.

Parameter Meaning
data_paths, data_labels HDF5 response files and their labels, in matching order. Each file can contain observations or simulations.
trial_queries, labels Trial selections and condition names in matching order. The queries apply to every file. Use [None] and ["All lists"] for one unfiltered condition.
comparison "datasets" compares files separately for each condition. "conditions" compares conditions from one file on the same axes.
complete_lists_only Exclude lists with a padded study position before applying the analysis.
max_subjects Maximum participants per file, starting with the lowest IDs. Zero includes everyone.
category_field Study-position field giving each item’s category when deriving the lookup from the observations.
category_features_path Optional NumPy category lookup indexed by global item ID minus one.
feature_column Zero-based category column when the supplied lookup is two-dimensional.
feature_label Name of the grouping feature used to label the transitions.
confidence_level, plot_seed Coverage and random seed for bootstrap intervals across participants.
project_root Base directory for relative input and output paths.
output_dir, figure_dir Output folder and optional separate folder for figures.
figure_str Figure filename stem. Use an empty string to display figures without saving them.
color_cycle, contrast_name Colors in display order and an optional legend title.
ylim, yticks Optional vertical-axis limits and tick locations.

Figures are saved under results/catcrp/ by default. A single figure uses the supplied stem (category_crp by default). Multiple figures add a number and the comparison title to each filename.

Analysis reference

Configure this run

Input files, selections, and analysis settings 
from typing import Literal

type ComparisonMode = Literal["conditions", "datasets"]

data_paths = ["data/Dupertuys2026.h5"]
data_labels = ["Observed"]
trial_queries = ["data['list_type'] == 1"]
labels = ["Mixed lists"]
comparison: ComparisonMode = "datasets"
complete_lists_only = False
max_subjects = 0

category_field: str = "valence"
category_features_path = None
feature_column = 6
feature_label = "Relation to preceding recall"
confidence_level = 0.95
plot_seed = 0

project_root = None
output_dir = "results/catcrp"
figure_dir = None
figure_str = "category_crp"
color_cycle = None
contrast_name = None
ylim = None
yticks = None

Load data and select trials

Relative paths use the project directory. The data guide describes the expected file format.

Install JAXCMR in Colab 
import sys

if "google.colab" in sys.modules:
    %pip install --upgrade "jaxcmr @ git+https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr.git@main"
Import analysis and plotting functions 
import re

import jax.numpy as jnp
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from jaxcmr.analyses.distcrp import plot_cat_crp
from jaxcmr.dataset import _require_pres_itemids, select_conditions
from jaxcmr.examples import copy_example_inputs
from jaxcmr.helpers import load_data, resolve_project_path, resolve_project_root
from jaxcmr.plotting import add_analysis_legend, comparison_panels, save_figure
Load response files 
root = resolve_project_root(project_root)
copy_example_inputs(
    data_paths + ([category_features_path] if category_features_path else []),
    base_dir=root,
)
datasets = [
    load_data(resolve_project_path(path, root), max_subjects=max_subjects)
    for path in data_paths
]
Reusing matching input: data/Dupertuys2026.h5
Select trials for each condition 
masks_by_dataset = []
for dataset in datasets:
    selections = select_conditions(
        dataset, trial_queries, complete_lists_only=complete_lists_only
    )
    masks_by_dataset.append([selection.mask for selection in selections])

Match item IDs to categories

A global item ID must have the same category wherever it appears in the selected lists. An external lookup can supply those categories directly.

Build the category lookup for the selected items 
category_features = (
    np.load(resolve_project_path(category_features_path, root))
    if category_features_path
    else None
)
if category_features is not None and category_features.ndim == 2:
    category_features = category_features[:, feature_column]

ids_blocks, category_blocks = [], []
for dataset, masks in zip(datasets, masks_by_dataset):
    selected = np.logical_or.reduce([np.asarray(mask) for mask in masks])
    ids = np.asarray(_require_pres_itemids(dataset))[selected].astype(int)
    categories = (
        category_features[np.maximum(ids - 1, 0)]
        if category_features is not None
        else np.asarray(dataset.get(category_field))[selected]
    )
    if categories.shape != ids.shape or not np.isfinite(categories[ids > 0]).all():
        raise ValueError("Supply one finite category per valid study item.")
    ids_blocks.append(ids[ids > 0])
    category_blocks.append(categories[ids > 0])

ids = np.concatenate(ids_blocks)
categories = np.concatenate(category_blocks)
category_values = np.unique(categories)
category_by_item = np.full(int(ids.max()), np.nan)
for item_id in np.unique(ids):
    values = np.unique(categories[ids == item_id])
    if len(values) != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Item {item_id} has conflicting categories across the selected inputs."
        )
    category_by_item[item_id - 1] = np.searchsorted(category_values, values[0])

Plot transitions within and between categories

Within-category and between-category transitions have separate opportunity counts. The points average participant probabilities for each transition type.

Draw and save each comparison 
panels = comparison_panels(
    datasets,
    masks_by_dataset,
    data_labels,
    labels,
    mode=comparison,
    selection_label=data_labels[0],
)
for number, panel in enumerate(panels, start=1):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4 if len(panel["labels"]) > 1 else 4.8, 3.2))
    plot_cat_crp(
        panel["datasets"],
        panel["trial_masks"],
        features=jnp.asarray(category_by_item),
        feature_label=feature_label,
        axis=ax,
        labels=panel["labels"],
        color_cycle=color_cycle,
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        bootstrap_seed=plot_seed,
    )
    title = panel["title"]
    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=12)
    if len(panel["labels"]) > 1:
        add_analysis_legend(ax, contrast_name)
    if ylim is not None:
        ax.set_ylim(ylim)
    if yticks is not None:
        ax.set_yticks(yticks)

    if figure_str:
        suffix = None
        if len(panels) > 1:
            label = re.sub(r"\W+", "_", title.casefold()).strip("_")
            suffix = f"{number}_{label}".rstrip("_")
        save_figure(
            resolve_project_path(figure_dir or output_dir, root),
            figure_str,
            suffix=suffix,
            figure=fig,
        )
    else:
        fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)
